title: Monomial filtration and composition length of a truncated monoid completion
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for the powers of $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $P$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid of a free abelian group $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$, where $r\ge0$, and let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism strictly positive on $P\setminus\{0\}$. Write $A[P]= igoplus_{p\in P}Az^p$, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, set $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak m,z^p:p
e0)$ and $B=\varprojlim_n A[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $p
e0$ let $
u(p)$ be the largest integer $q$ for which $p=p_1+\cdots+p_q$ with each $p_i\in P\setminus\{0\}$, and put $
u(0)=0$. For every integer $n\ge1$, the set $S_n=\{p\in P:
u(p)<n\}$ is finite. Choose any isomorphism $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$, order $P$ lexicographically by $(w(p),p_1,\ldots,p_r)$, and write $S_n=\{t_1<\cdots<t_N\}$. Identify $B/\mathfrak b^nB$ as an $A$-module with $ igoplus_{p\in S_n}A/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(p)}$ by its coefficients. For $1\le j\le N$ let $F_j$ consist of the classes whose coefficients at $t_1,\ldots,t_{j-1}$ vanish, and set $F_{N+1}=0$. Then $F_1=B/\mathfrak b^nB$ and every $F_j$ is a $B$-submodule. The coefficient at $t_j$ induces an isomorphism $F_j/F_{j+1}\cong A/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(t_j)}$ of $B$-modules, where the action on the right is through the constant-coefficient homomorphism $c:B	o A$. On each such factor the $B$-submodules are exactly the $A$-submodules. Every $A/\mathfrak m^k$, $k\ge1$, and every $B/\mathfrak b^nB$ has finite composition length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and
$$\mathrm{length}_B(B/\mathfrak b^nB)=\sum_{
u(p)<n}\mathrm{length}_A(A/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(p)}).$$

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficients] to the given $A,P,G,w$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed Noetherian locality, completeness, finite generation, embedding and positive weight. It supplies the finite set $S_n$, the coefficient ring $B=A^P$ with finite convolution sums, and the stated coefficient identification of $B/\mathfrak b^nB$. In particular every quotient class has a representative which is a finite sum supported on $S_n$: lift its finitely many residue coefficients to $A$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76): agent-supplied monomial-filtration refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: In the coefficient ring of step 1 put $c(b)=b_0$. If $u+v=0$ with $u,v\in P$, positivity of $w$ forces $u=v=0$. Thus convolution gives $c(bb')=c(b)c(b')$, so $c$ is a ring homomorphism. Constants give a section $A\to B$ of $c$. The specified lexicographic order is a total order, and $u+v>u$ whenever $v\ne0$, since $w(v)>0$. List the finite $S_n$ in this order. Its first element is $0$, and it is nonempty because $\nu(0)=0<n$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76): agent-supplied monomial-filtration refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: Fix $j\le N$ and $x\in F_j$. Choose the representative $f=\sum_{i=j}^N a_i z^{t_i}$: its earlier residue coefficients vanish, so they can be lifted as zero. For $b\in B$ and $t\in S_n$ with $t\le t_j$, the convolution coefficient of $bf$ sums over $t_i+v=t$, $i\ge j$. For $v\ne0$ this would give $t>t_i\ge t_j$, impossible. Only $v=0$, $t_i=t$ remains. Consequently all coefficients below $t_j$ vanish and the coefficient at $t_j$ is $c(b)a_j$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{n-\nu(t_j)}$. Addition and additive inverses preserve the vanishing conditions. Hence $F_j$ is a $B$-submodule; $F_1$ is the whole quotient and $F_{N+1}=0$ is a submodule.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76): agent-supplied monomial-filtration refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: The coefficient map $F_j\to A/\mathfrak m^{n-\nu(t_j)}$ is $B$-linear by step 3, where $B$ acts through $c$. Its kernel is exactly $F_{j+1}$. It is onto, since the class of $az^{t_j}$ maps to the residue of any $a\in A$. An explicit inverse on the quotient sends this residue to $[az^{t_j}]$ modulo $F_{j+1}$; changing $a$ by the displayed ideal gives zero in the coefficient quotient of step 1. This proves the claimed factor isomorphism. For any additive subgroup of the factor, stability under $A$ implies stability under $B$ because $b$ acts as $c(b)$, and stability under $B$ implies stability under $A$ using constants. The submodule lattices therefore coincide, including all their strict chains; their lengths agree by [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76): agent-supplied monomial-filtration refinement, not a theorem stated in ILO.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge] with $R=A$; its hypotheses hold since $A$ is a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring. It gives finite $A$-length for every $A/\mathfrak m^k$, $k\ge1$. Put $k_j=n-\nu(t_j)\ge1$. Step 4 gives $\mathrm{length}_B(F_j/F_{j+1})=\mathrm{length}_A(A/\mathfrak m^{k_j})<\infty$. Starting with $F_{N+1}=0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] successively to $0\to F_{j+1}\to F_j\to F_j/F_{j+1}\to0$, for $j=N,\ldots,1$. The inclusion is injective, the quotient map is surjective, and its kernel is $F_{j+1}$. Induction gives finite length and the sum of the factor lengths for $F_1=B/\mathfrak b^nB$, as asserted.
